annotations.title: The idols of the Gentiles are siluer and gold.
annotations.text: Al Catholique Diuines agree in this authentical definition, of Idolatrie, <mn>[1]</mn> that it is diuine honour geuen to anie creature, as to a god. Of the diuers sortes also of Idolatrie the ancient lerned Doctors haue written much. <mn>[2]</mn> Namely Iustinus Martyr in his Orations against the Gentiles, Tertullian in Apologetico, Arnobius Orat. ad Gentes. Lactantius, li. 1. c. 17. Diuinar. Instit. and manie others. But most copiously and profoundly S. Augustin, especially in his tenne first bookes de Ciuitate Dei. Into which error & crime the Platonistes fel, holding that spiritual inuisible created substances, to witte, Angels good and euil, <mn>[3]</mn> whom they called Intelligentias separatas, had diuine powre, & so gaue to them diuine honour. Others honour dead men, and some before their death as goddes, for their notable actes atchieued in this life, as Saturne, Iuppiter, Hercules, and the like. Some yeld diuine honour to mere corporal creatures, <mn>[4]</mn> liuing or without life, as to beastes and serpentes, the sunne, the moone, fire, water, earth, the whole machin of the world, as if it were animate, and that with diuine spirite or soule. Againe al these haue bene worshipped as gods, <mn>[5]</mn> not only in them selues but also in their imagees. But to omite other diuersities, the most grosse sorte of al, is the Idolatrie which the Psalmist here describeth, when Imagees made by mens handes are immediatly honored as goddes in themselues. <mn>[6]</mn> For such goddes the Gentiles had, and of them the Prophet here speaketh. Comparing these visible sensles imagined goddes, <mn>[7]</mn>with the one eternal inuisible God, who is made notorious by his diuine conspicuous workes, wheras these idols, by how much they are more visible, so much more they are contemptible: because being fashioned with mouth, eyes, eares, nose, handes, feete, throte, and other members, they are altogether sensles, not able to speake with their mouth, and therin more base in nature, then the men that made them; nor able to see, heare, smel, taist, feele, to walke, to moue, nor to crie, al which beastes can doe. And therfore those that make them, or haue confidence in them (as the Prophet here signifieth that some haue. v. 16.) are most absurde: becoming like to the same idols, in their vnderstanding and internal cogitations, as these idols are voide of external sense. <mn>[8]</mn> And al Idolaters are most wicked, geuing diuine honour to anie creature, & are therin seruantes of diuels: <mn>[9]</mn> Whether they immediatly honour diuels, as when sorcerers and witches, making pact with the diuel, adore him, and he for the same doth some thing which they demand: or that they honour some other creature, wherin by the diuels false persuasion, they thincke there is diuine powre. Both which waies diuels vsurpe Gods honour and therfore the same Prophet saide in an other <mn>[10]</mn> Psalme: Al the goddes of Gentiles are diuels.

notes.text: Corporal creatures, sensible and without sense.
